posts.text: A vulture's stomach acid sits near pH zero. It destroys anthrax and botulism before either one gets near the bloodstream.
comments: Which is how a bird eats week-old roadkill and walks away fine. Built-in hazmat suit.

posts.text: The slow loris licks a gland on the inside of its elbow, mixes the secretion into its saliva, then bites. Only venomous primate we know of.
comments: That bite can put a person into anaphylactic shock. The cute face is doing a lot of work here.

posts.text: Woodpeckers hammer 20 times a second and never concuss. Not because the skull cushions anything, a 2022 study killed that idea. It stays rigid so they can hit harder.
comments: The real reason they survive it is that the brain is tiny, so each impact is over too fast to do damage.

posts.text: On a moonless night a dung beetle looks up, takes a mental snapshot of the Milky Way, and uses it to roll in a straight line.
comments: Only insect known to navigate by the galaxy. Send this to whoever thinks insects are simple, the fact card is here → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/steered-by-the-milky-way/

posts.text: A capybara can hold its breath for five minutes with only its eyes, ears, and nostrils above the waterline, hippo style. Any keepers seen one do the full submarine?
comments: It is a jaguar and caiman avoidance system, not a spa treatment.

posts.text: Komodo dragons do not kill with filthy mouths. They have real venom glands that stop blood from clotting and crash the victim's blood pressure.
comments: The bacteria story ran for decades before anyone actually checked. When they do land a meal they can eat 80 percent of their own body weight in one sitting.

posts.text: A secretary bird hunts venomous snakes on foot, kicking with up to five times its own body weight and resetting for the next strike in a fraction of a second.
comments: The absurd legs are the whole point. They keep the body out of biting range while the stomping happens.

posts.text: A seahorse has no stomach at all. Food goes straight through, so it has to graze almost constantly just to stay alive. Anyone here actually kept them long term?
comments: Some species put away thousands of tiny shrimp a day. Full fact card if you want the rest of it → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/no-stomach-no-problem/

posts.text: The basenji cannot bark. Its larynx is shaped wrong for it, so it yodels instead, a sound owners call the baroo. Anyone here live with one?
comments: Barkless on paper. Nobody who owns one describes them as quiet.

posts.text: A bar-tailed godwit was tracked flying over 13,000 km from Alaska to Australia. No food, no water, no landing.
comments: Longest nonstop flight ever recorded for any bird, done in a single go.

posts.text: Some glass frogs are transparent enough underneath that you can watch the heart beating through the skin.
comments: While they sleep they pack nearly all their red blood cells into the liver, which makes them even harder to pick out against a leaf.

posts.text: A protein pulled from Gila monster venom, exendin-4, became the basis for early diabetes drugs and later helped inspire the GLP-1 medications behind Ozempic.
comments: It is also the only venomous lizard native to the US, living off tail fat between a few meals a year. Worth sending to anyone who thinks venom research is a dead end → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/from-venom-to-ozempic/

posts.text: A starfish has no brain and no blood. Faced with something too big to swallow, it pushes its own stomach out through its mouth and digests the meal outside its body.
comments: The whole animal runs on seawater, pumped through hundreds of little hydraulic tube feet.

posts.text: A wolverine's upper molar is set about 90 degrees sideways, which turns the back of its jaw into a shearing tool.
comments: That one rotated tooth is how a 15 kilogram animal opens a carcass frozen solid, the kind bigger scavengers walk away from.

posts.text: Wood frogs freeze solid through winter. The heart stops, the blood stops moving, and up to 65 percent of the body's water turns to ice.
comments: Then spring arrives, they thaw, and they hop off like nothing happened.

posts.text: Coconut crab claws have been measured pinching at over 3,000 newtons, a grip in the same range as a lion's bite.
comments: Largest land arthropod alive, and it cracks coconuts with that. Send it to whoever thinks the spider in the bathroom is the problem → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/grip-like-a-lions-bite/

posts.text: Red pandas grip bamboo with a false thumb, an extended wrist bone doing the job of a digit. Giant pandas evolved the same fix independently.
comments: Two animals that are not close relatives at all, landing on the identical solution to the identical problem.

posts.text: The basilisk lizard sprints across open water on its hind legs, up to 20 steps a second, riding air pockets its own toes create. Anyone with one seen it happen in person?
comments: It gets roughly 20 meters before physics catches up and it drops into a swim.

posts.text: A well fed vampire bat will bring up blood to feed a hungry roost-mate, but usually only one that has shared with it before.
comments: Skip your turn and the colony remembers. Bookkeeping, with fangs.

posts.text: A kiwi egg can weigh a fifth of the mother's body weight. An ostrich egg is about 2 percent of hers.
comments: Kiwis are also the only birds with nostrils at the tip of the beak, for sniffing out grubs underground. Whole card is here if you want it → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-impossible-egg/

posts.text: Filmed side by side, biting flies came at zebras and horses at the same rate but landed on the zebras less than a quarter as often. Anyone tried a striped fly sheet on a horse?
comments: Best supported explanation is that the hard black and white contrast wrecks a fly's ability to slow down and land.

posts.text: A Gaboon viper's fangs run about five centimeters, longer than any other snake's, folded flat against the roof of the mouth until the strike swings them forward.
comments: Its venom is not the most potent by weight. The dose is what makes a bite serious.

posts.text: The barreleye fish has a transparent dome for a head, with its two tubular eyes sitting visible right through the shield.
comments: Everyone assumed those eyes were fixed looking up. A 2009 study showed the fish rotates them forward to track food drifting past its mouth.

posts.text: Kea are the only alpine parrots on earth, and they strip the rubber trim off parked cars for entertainment. What is the boldest thing a wild bird has taken off you?
comments: They also out-solve some primates in lab tests. Researchers think the vandalism is how they learn. Full card → https://beastlyfacts.com/facts/the-alpine-kleptomaniac/

posts.text: The kangaroo rat never drinks. It pulls every bit of water it needs out of the dry seeds it eats.
comments: A desert animal that solved hydration by opting out of it entirely.
